passages.text: All statements in this section, other than statements of historical fact, are forward-looking statements that are inherently uncertain. See “Disclosures Regarding Forward-Looking Statements” and Item 1A. Risk Factors for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected in these statements. The following information concerning our business, results of operations and financial condition should also be read in conjunction with the information included under Item 1. Business, Item 1A. Risk Factors and Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY Business Update Our Refining & Marketing segment results for 2025 versus 2024 reflect higher realized refining margins supported by stable demand and by gasoline and distillate inventory levels in the U.S. that were at or below five-year averages. Longer term, global demand growth is expected to outpace the net impact of refining capacity additions and rationalizations through the end of the decade. We anticipate these fundamentals, as well as the U.S. refining industry’s current structural advantages over the rest of the world, will support a constructive environment for U.S. refiners. Our Midstream segment contributed strong results and continued growth in 2025, benefitting from the expansion of its Permian to Gulf Coast natural gas and NGL value chains with the Northwind Midstream Acquisition and the BANGL Acquisition, progression of long-haul pipeline growth projects and expansion of Gulf Coast fractionation and export facilities. We believe our Midstream business is well positioned and has significant opportunities to support the development plans of its producer customers. In response to the current business environment, we continue to focus on the following priorities for our business: Commitment to Safety, Reliability and Sustainability We remain steadfast in our commitment to safely and reliably operate our assets and protect the health and safety of our employees. We are focused on sustainable structural changes to improve our cost competitiveness while maintaining safe and reliable operations. Our approach to sustainability spans the environmental, social and governance dimensions of our business. That means strengthening resiliency by lowering the carbon intensity and conserving natural resources; innovating for the future by investing in renewables and emerging technologies; and embedding sustainability in decision-making and in how we engage our people and many stakeholders. We have existing targets for reducing Scope 1 & 2 GHG emissions intensity, for lowering methane emissions intensity and for lowering our freshwater withdrawal intensity. Operational Excellence We are committed to achieving operational excellence by reducing costs, improving efficiency, driving operational improvements and being disciplined in capital allocation. This means lowering our costs in all aspects of our business and challenging ourselves to be disciplined in every dollar we spend across our organization. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: You should carefully consider each of the following risks and all the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K in evaluating us and our common stock. Although the risks are organized by headings, and each risk is discussed separately, many are interrelated. Our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows could be materially and adversely affected by these risks, and, as a result, the trading price of our common stock could decline. We have in the past been adversely affected by certain of, and may in the future be affected by, these risks. Business and Operational Risks Our financial results are affected by volatile refining margins, which are dependent on factors beyond our control. Our operating results, cash flows, future rate of growth, the carrying value of our assets and our ability to execute share repurchases and pay our dividend at intended levels are highly dependent on the margins we realize on our refined products. Historically, refined product margins have been volatile, and we believe they will continue to be volatile. Our margins from the sale of refined products are influenced by a number of conditions, including the price of crude oil and other feedstocks. The prices of feedstocks and the prices at which we can sell our refined products fluctuate independently due to a variety of regional and global market factors that are beyond our control, including: • global and regional inventory levels and availability of and demand for feedstocks and refined products; • transportation infrastructure cost and availability; • temporary and permanent closures, utilization levels and capacities of other refineries in our markets and globally; • global and regional development by competitors of new refining or renewable conversion capacity; • natural gas and electricity availability and supply costs; • global and domestic political instability, threatened or actual terrorist incidents, armed conflict, economic activity and growth levels or lack thereof or other global political or economic conditions; • tariffs on goods, including crude oil and other feedstocks, imported into the United States; • local weather conditions; and • the occurrence of other risks described herein. Some of these factors can vary by region and may change quickly, adding to market volatility, while others may have longer-term effects. The longer-term effects of these and other factors on refined product margins are uncertain. We generally purchase our feedstocks weeks before we refine them and sell the refined products. Price level changes during the period between purchasing feedstocks and selling the refined products from these feedstocks can have a significant effect on our financial results. We also purchase refined products manufactured by others for resale to our customers. Price changes during the periods between purchasing and reselling those refined products can have a material and adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital spending, leaving free cash flow that supports debt service and distributions. The refining and midstream asset base generates recurring cash despite margin volatility, and the midstream segment's fee-based growth adds stability. This internally funded model reduces reliance on external financing for routine capital needs.

Interest coverage remains solid, with operating income covering gross interest expense multiple times over. The company's scale and integrated refining and midstream operations provide earnings diversity, while the current ratio indicates adequate near-term liquidity. These factors support the issuer's ability to meet fixed obligations through the cycle.

key_risks.text: Refining margins are highly volatile and driven by factors beyond management's control, including global inventory levels, feedstock prices, and geopolitical events. The risk-factor passage explicitly notes that operating results, cash flows, and the ability to fund buybacks and dividends at intended levels depend on realized refined product margins, which have historically fluctuated and are expected to remain volatile.

Debt maturities are concentrated in the near term, with a substantial portion due within the next twelve months and the following year. This refinancing requirement, combined with the company's significant capital spending and shareholder distributions, could strain liquidity if cash flows weaken. The debt structure includes both long-term borrowings and current debt, necessitating active liability management.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow to debt remains modest, indicating that internally generated funds cover only a limited portion of the debt stack annually. While operating cash flow is substantial, capital expenditures and shareholder returns absorb a significant share, leaving a thin margin for debt reduction. This ratio trails sector norms, suggesting reliance on refinancing or asset sales to manage maturities.

Net leverage sits above the sector median, reflecting the company's sizable debt load relative to earnings. Although interest coverage is adequate, the elevated leverage reduces financial flexibility and increases vulnerability to margin downturns. The indicative risk profile is significant, with limited headroom before breaching higher-risk thresholds.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer's credit profile is supported by strong operating cash flow and solid interest coverage, but tempered by above-median leverage and volatile refining margins. The midstream segment provides some earnings stability, yet the core refining business remains cyclical. Shareholder distributions and acquisitions absorb most free cash flow, limiting deleveraging capacity.

Looking forward, the company's ability to manage near-term maturities and maintain distributions will depend on refining margin recovery and disciplined capital allocation. The indicative financial risk profile is significant, and leverage headroom is limited. A sustained margin downturn could pressure metrics, while successful midstream growth and cost controls could support gradual improvement.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，留下自由現金流支持償債及分派。儘管利潤率波動，煉油及中游資產基礎仍產生經常性現金，而中游分部的收費式增長增添穩定性。此內部融資模式減少對外部融資的依賴以應付日常資本需求。
利息覆蓋率維持穩健，營運收入足以覆蓋總利息開支多倍。公司規模及綜合煉油與中游業務提供盈利多元化，而流動比率顯示短期流動性充足。這些因素支持發行人於週期內履行固定責任的能力。

key_risks.text: 煉油利潤率高度波動，並受管理層無法控制的因素驅動，包括全球庫存水平、原料價格及地緣政治事件。風險因素段落明確指出，經營業績、現金流及按預期水平為回購和股息提供資金的能力取決於已實現的成品油利潤率，該利潤率歷來波動，並預計將持續波動。
債務到期集中於短期，其中相當部分將於未來十二個月及隨後一年內到期。此再融資需求，加上公司龐大的資本開支及股東分派，可能在現金流減弱時對流動性構成壓力。債務結構包括長期借款及流動債務，需要積極的負債管理。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流對債務比率仍然適中，顯示內部產生的資金每年僅覆蓋債務總額的有限部分。儘管營運現金流可觀，資本開支及股東回報佔據顯著份額，留下微薄的債務削減空間。此比率落後於行業常規，表明依賴再融資或資產出售來管理到期債務。
淨槓桿率高於行業中位數，反映公司相對於盈利的龐大債務負擔。儘管利息覆蓋率充足，較高的槓桿率降低財務靈活性，並增加對利潤率下行的脆弱性。指示性風險狀況顯著，在觸及較高風險門檻前緩衝有限。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人的信用狀況受強勁營運現金流及穩健利息覆蓋率支持，但受高於中位數的槓桿率及波動的煉油利潤率所抑制。中游分部提供部分盈利穩定性，惟核心煉油業務仍具週期性。股東分派及收購吸收大部分自由現金流，限制去槓桿能力。
展望未來，公司管理短期到期債務及維持分派的能力將取決於煉油利潤率復甦及嚴謹的資本配置。指示性財務風險狀況顯著，槓桿緩衝有限。利潤率持續下行可能對指標構成壓力，而成功的中游增長及成本控制可支持逐步改善。
